items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A real-outcome observational experiment with a finite discrete confounder. One full-data unit is \((X,A,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\) with \(X\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(A\in\{0,1\}\) and real potential outcomes; the law \(P\) is determined by the cell masses \(p_k=P(X=k)\), the propensities \(\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k)\), and the arm-and-cell conditional outcome laws on \(\mathbb R\). Consistency \(Y=Y(A)\) and conditional exchangeability \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X\) hold, treatment satisfies fixed strong overlap \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass cell, and the outcome is controlled only through \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M/2\) and \(E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le M^2\); no boundedness of \(Y\) is assumed. The observed record is \(O=(X,A,Y)\) with law \(P_O\), and the sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) is drawn from \(Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}\), with the same product construction at block size \(m\). — Search trace: read `grep '^## ' ../doc/API.md` section index and §8h `PO/`, §12 `Stat/`, §13sa `Estimation/MinimaxATE/`, §10z reusable minimax substrate; then `Glob CausalSmith/Stat/**/*.lean` and `lean_file_outline` on `CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_DiscreteAteMinimaxLoggap_Research/Basic.lean`. Result: the closest world is `CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteAteMinimaxLoggap.DiscreteLaw` / `Obs d` (see S2), but that world is a PMF on `Fin d x Bool x Bool` -- a BINARY outcome. The frozen core is stated for real outcomes controlled only by a conditional second central moment (`ass:second-central-moment`), so the binary world is a strictly different abstraction and cannot carry the class; `Causalean/PO/` supplies measure-theoretic PO systems over general outcome spaces but no finite-cell arbitrary-mass discrete-confounder law with per-cell arm outcome measures. Mathlib side checked with `lean_leansearch` ('expectation of one over binomial count plus one') -- only `PMF.binomial`/`PMF.bernoulli`, no packaged experiment. Hence `bypass-justified`: local record type carrying `p : Fin d -> R`, `pi : Fin d -> R`, and `nu : Bool -> Fin d -> Measure R`, with `productLaw` built by `Measure.pi`, reusing Causalean's `Stat.Sample` product plumbing. The full-data layer adds the joint potential-outcome law used by `ass:consistency` / `ass:conditional-exchangeability`.

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: The binary-outcome discrete-confounder experiment of Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han and Kennedy: one unit is \((X,A,B)\) with \(X\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and \(A,B\in\{0,1\}\), arbitrary cell masses, fixed overlap \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\), arm response means \(\eta_{ak}\in[0,1]\), and an \(n\)-fold product sampling law. This is the source experiment for the cited converse lemmas, and the affine map \(B(a)\mapsto M\{B(a)-1/2\}\) together with the Bernoulli contraction channel embeds it into the ambient world \(S1\). — Highest-leverage reuse decision in the plan. The banked sibling paper `stat_discrete_ate_minimax_loggap_polynomial_upper_match` already formalizes exactly this binary source world: `DiscreteLaw d`, `Obs d`, `Overlap`, `Consistency`, `ConditionalExchangeability`, `observedMarginal`, `ateFunctional`, `productLaw`, `mse`, `worstCaseMSE`, `minimaxRisk`, `oneArmMinimaxRisk`, `ControlZeroLaw`, and the cited-gate Prop `ZengOneArmMinimaxLower` (verified by `lean_file_outline` on Basic.lean and `Grep ZengOneArmMinimaxLower` in Helpers/LowerBound.lean). Every binary-source lemma of the present core is stated in this world, so the embedding lemmas (`prop:zeng-class-inclusion-and-lower-transfer`, `lem:scaled-binary-exact-lower-transfer-all-d`, `thm:radius-channel-converse-all-d`) are bridges from S2 to S1 rather than fresh constructions.

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}:=\{P: X\in\{1,\ldots,d\},\ A\in\{0,1\},\ Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\mathbb R,\ 0<\epsilon<1/2,\ M\ge1,\ 0\le\sigma\le2,\text{ and }P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:overlap},\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}normalization},\mathrm{ass:second\text{-}central\text{-}moment},\mathrm{ass:approximate\text{-}homogeneity}\}\).

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}:=\{P: X\in\{1,\ldots,d\},\ A\in\{0,1\},\ Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\mathbb R,\ 0<\epsilon<1/2,\ M\ge1,\text{ and }P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:overlap},\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}normalization},\mathrm{ass:second\text{-}central\text{-}moment}\}\).

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl: Split the observations into two independent blocks \(I_0\) and \(I_1\).  The block \(I_0\) is used only to classify cells as heavy or light by empirical occupancy.  On light cells, use fixed shifted-Chebyshev coefficients of degree proportional to \(\log(en)\), evaluated on \(I_1\) by ordered distinct-index falling-factorial statistics carrying exactly one normalized outcome mark.  On heavy cells, use indicator-totalized arm sample-mean differences on \(I_1\), weighted by the \(I_1\) empirical cell frequency.  Sum the light and heavy contributions, multiply by \(M\), and clip to \([-M,M]\).  Set the estimator to zero outside the calibrated range.  The constants, degree, occupancy threshold, positive-denominator indicators, and fallbacks are those in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}ratio\text{-}polynomial\text{-}upper}\).

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl:
From \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), let \(N_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}\), \(N_k:=N_{0k}+N_{1k}\), \(S_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}Y_i\), \(I_k:=\mathbf 1\{N_{0k}N_{1k}>0\}\), and \(R_n:=\sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k\).  Put \(\overline Y_{ak}:=S_{ak}/N_{ak}\) when \(N_{ak}>0\), and define
\[
 T_n^{\mathrm{col}}:=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}\!\left(
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}
 \sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k(\overline Y_{1k}-\overline Y_{0k})
 \right),
\]
with the inner value defined to be zero when \(R_n=0\).  The map is total, measurable, and computable by one pass through the sample followed by one pass through the occupied categories.

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl: For \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\), let \(u_{n,d}:=d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\), \(h_{n,d,\sigma}:=\sigma^2+d/n^2\), and define \[\widehat\tau_n^{\star}:=\begin{cases}T_n^{\mathrm{col}},&h_{n,d,\sigma}\le\min\{1,u_{n,d}\},\\T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},&u_{n,d}<\min\{1,h_{n,d,\sigma}\},\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] The displayed tie rule makes the selector a total measurable map for every \((n,d,\sigma)\).

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl:
Let \(\lambda:=\sigma/2\).  Start from a fixed-sample binary one-arm hard family with at most \(d_{\mathrm{rad}}:=\min\{d,\max(1,\lfloor b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}}n\log(en)\rfloor)\}\) positive-mass cells, assign zero mass to unused cells, and pass each binary potential response through the hypothesis-independent kernel
\[
 B(a)\longmapsto B'(a)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left\{\frac12+\lambda\left(B(a)-\frac12\right)\right\},
 \qquad Y(a):=M\{B'(a)-1/2\}.
\]
For the exact-homogeneity component, scale a uniform-mass binary hard family on at most \(d_{\mathrm{ex}}:=\min\{d,\max(1,\lfloor b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}n^2\rfloor)\}\) positive-mass cells by \(B(a)\mapsto M\{B(a)-1/2\}\), again assigning zero mass to unused cells.  Here \(b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}},b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}>0\) are fixed constants depending only on \(\epsilon\).  This construction handle names only the two embedded families and the channel; class membership, target separation, data processing, finite-sample cutoffs, and the resulting capped all-alphabet risk bounds are proved separately.

items.label: Definition P-10
items.nl:
Put \(L:=\log(en)\), \(b:=n^{-1}+d/n^2\), and \(u:=d^2/(n^2L^2)\).  In the only residual shrinking-radius wedge
\[
 b\ll u\ll1,
 \qquad
 b\ll\sigma^2\ll1,
\]
equivalently up to boundary constants \(\sqrt n\,L\ll d\ll nL\) and \(\sigma^2\gg b\), can one either construct a realization-wise radius-constrained paired-cell moment-matching fuzzy experiment in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) having ATE separation of order
\[
 M\min\left\{\sigma,\frac{d}{nL}\right\}
\]
and sample-mixture total variation bounded away from one, or construct an explicit total estimator whose risk is strictly smaller in order than the selector benchmark \(M^2\{b+\min(u,\sigma^2)\}\), ideally attaining the proved product benchmark \(M^2(b+\sigma^2u)\)?  The existing hypothesis-independent channel gives only the product separation
\[
 M\sigma\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{nL}\right\},
\]
so reusing that channel does not answer the question in this residual wedge.

items.label: Assumption A-4
items.nl: \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M/2\) for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

items.label: Assumption A-6
items.nl: \(E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le M^2\) for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: Every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) satisfies \(|\tau_k|\le M\), \(|\tau(P)|\le M\), and \(\max_{k:p_k>0}|\delta_k|\le2M\). Consequently \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}=\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\).

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\ge c_{\epsilon}M^2/n\) for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and every \(d,n\ge1\).

items.label: Lemma lem:zeng-binary-exact-homogeneity-lower
items.nl:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  Let \(\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) be the fixed-sample binary-outcome experiment with \(p_k=1/d\), \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\), conditional response means in \([0,1]\), and a common cell treatment effect, and write \(\psi(P):=d^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^d(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\).  There are constants \(a_{\epsilon},b_{\epsilon}>0\) and \(N_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that, for \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\) and \(d\le b_{\epsilon}n^2\),
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)}
 E_P[(\widehat\psi-\psi(P))^2]
 \ge a_{\epsilon}\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:zeng-binary-one-arm-lower
items.nl:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  In the fixed-sample binary-outcome model with arbitrary cell masses, overlap \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\), arbitrary treated response means in \([0,1]\), and control response identically zero, constants \(a_{\epsilon},b_{\epsilon}>0\) and \(N_{\epsilon}<\infty\) satisfy, for \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\) and \(d\le b_{\epsilon}n\log n\),
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_P E_P[(\widehat\psi-\sum_{k=1}^dp_k\mu_{1k})^2]
 \ge a_{\epsilon}\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2 n}\right\}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:zeng-usable-occupancy-reciprocal
items.nl:
For \(N_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}\), \(N_k:=N_{0k}+N_{1k}\), \(I_k:=\mathbf 1\{N_{0k}N_{1k}>0\}\), and \(R_n:=\sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k\), fixed overlap implies that constants \(b_{\epsilon},B_{\epsilon}>0\) satisfy
\[
 Q_P^{(n)}(R_n=0)\le2\exp\left\{-b_{\epsilon}\frac{n^2}{n\vee d}\right\}
\]
and
\[
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\left[\frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}\right]
 \le B_{\epsilon}\left\{\frac{n\vee d}{n^2}+\exp\left(-b_{\epsilon}\frac{n^2}{n\vee d}\right)\right\}.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exists \(C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that the following holds.  Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), let \(V:=Y/M\), \(s_{ak}:=P(X=k,A=a)\), and \(z_{ak}:=E_P[V\mathbf 1\{X=k,A=a\}]\), and consider a block of \(m\) independent observations with joint law \(Q_P^{(m)}\).  For integers \(K\ge2\), numbers \(B>0\), and
\[
 g_{Kj}:=(-1)^j\frac{2^{2j+3}}{K(K+j+2)}\binom{K+j+2}{2j+4},\qquad 0\le j\le K-2,
\]
define the ordered, distinct-index statistic
\[
 U_{k,a,j}:=\frac{1}{(m)_{j+2}}
 \sum_{i_0,\ldots,i_{j+1}\ {\rm distinct}}
 V_{i_0}\mathbf 1\{X_{i_0}=k,A_{i_0}=a\}
 \mathbf 1\{X_{i_1}=k\}
 \prod_{t=2}^{j+1}\mathbf 1\{X_{i_t}=k,A_{i_t}=a\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat P_k:=\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}\frac{g_{Kj}}{B^{j+1}}
 \{U_{k,1,j}-U_{k,0,j}\}.
\]
If \(S\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B/4\}\) is deterministic, \(4(K+2)^2\le m\), and \(4(K+2)/m\le3B/4\), then
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{Q_P^{(m)}}\!\left(\sum_{k\in S}\widehat P_k\right)
 \le \frac{C_{\epsilon}}m+C_{\epsilon}6^{2K}
 \left\{dB^2+\frac{d^2K^2B^2}{m}\right\}.
\]
No boundedness of \(Y\) is required.

items.label: Lemma L-7
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the total occupancy-weighted estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:collision\text{-}handle}\) satisfies, for a constant \(C_{\epsilon}<\infty\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\frac1n+\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right)
\]
for every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\) and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\).  The claim requires only fixed overlap, the conditional-second-central-moment envelope, the mean normalization used for clipping, and approximate homogeneity; it remains valid when some cells have zero mass and on every empirical division boundary.

items.label: Lemma L-8
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are \(C_{\epsilon},\rho_{\epsilon}>0\) and \(N_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that the explicit heavy--light signed one-mark estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) specified by Definition~\(\mathrm{def:polynomial\text{-}handle}\), including its declared zero fallback when \(n<N_{\epsilon}\) or \(d>\rho_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), is a total element of \(\mathcal T_{n,M}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\frac1n+
 \min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}
\]
for every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\) and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\).  In its calibrated branch it uses \(O(dK^2)\) arithmetic operations after cell aggregation, and every branch has bounded fallbacks on every division boundary.

items.label: Lemma L-9
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is a constant \(c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that, for every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\) and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\),
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\frac1n+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
The capped alphabet term is obtained by embedding an exactly homogeneous binary hard experiment on \(d_0:=\min\{d,\max(1,\lfloor b_{\epsilon}n^2\rfloor)\}\) positive-mass cells and assigning zero mass to all unused cells, where \(b_{\epsilon}>0\) is a fixed source constant depending only on \(\epsilon\).

items.label: Lemma lem:binary-exact-collision-lower
items.nl:
Let \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), and set \(u_{\epsilon}:=\min\{1/2,\,8(1/2-\epsilon)^2\}\).  For every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\) with \(d\le n^2\), the minimax risk of the fixed-sample binary exactly homogeneous source experiment \(\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\), the \(n\)-fold independent experiment generated by binary laws whose cell masses are uniform, whose propensities lie in \([\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), and whose cell effect is the same in every cell, satisfies the collision-regime lower bound
\[
\frac{u_{\epsilon}^2}{64}\cdot\frac{d}{n^2}
\le
\inf_{\widehat\psi}\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\{\widehat\psi-\psi(P)\}^2\right],
\]
where the infimum runs over all measurable estimators \(\widehat\psi\) of the binary average response contrast \(\psi\).

items.label: Lemma lem:same-cell-factorial-cross-moment
Lemma lem:distinct-cell-factorial-cross-moment
items.nl:
Let \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), let \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, and let \(U_{k,a,j}\) be the ordered distinct-index one-mark factorial statistics on a block of \(m\) independent observations with joint law \(Q_P^{(m)}\), as in \cref{obj:lem:same-cell-factorial-cross-moment}.  If \(k\) and \(\ell\) are distinct cells, \(j+2\le K\), \(r+2\le K\), and \(4(K+2)^2\le m\), then for all arms \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\) only the disjoint-tuple normalization correction survives:
\[
\left|\operatorname{Cov}_{Q_P^{(m)}}\!\left(U_{k,a,j},U_{\ell,b,r}\right)\right|
\le
\frac{2(K+2)^2}{m}\,p_k^{j+2}p_{\ell}^{r+2}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:shifted-chebyshev-coefficient-envelope
items.nl:
Let \(K\ge1\) be an integer, let \(B>0\), and let
\[
g_{Kj}:=(-1)^j\frac{2^{2j+3}}{K(K+j+2)}\binom{K+j+2}{2j+4},
\qquad 0\le j\le K-2,
\]
be the shifted-Chebyshev coefficients.  Then every real \(p\) with \(0\le p\le B\) satisfies the coefficient envelope
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}\left|\frac{g_{Kj}}{B^{j+1}}\right|p^{j+2}
\le
B\,6^{K}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:polynomial-fixed-branch-risk
Lemma lem:capped-radial-transport-scale
items.nl:
Let \(a\ge0\) and \(0<b\le4\), let \(n\ge3\) and \(d\ge1\) be integers with \(1\le (b/2)\,n\log(en)\), and let
\[
d_{\mathrm{rad}}
:=
\min\left\{d,\ \max\left(1,\left\lfloor \frac b2\,n\log(en)\right\rfloor\right)\right\}
\]
be the capped radial alphabet size of \(\cref{obj:def:least-favorable-handle}\).  Then, for every \(M\) and every \(\sigma\),
\[
\frac{ab^2}{128}\,M^2\sigma^2\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}
\le
\left(\frac{M\sigma}{2}\right)^2
\frac a2
\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d_{\mathrm{rad}}^2}{n^2\log^2 n}\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, once the Bernoulli radius channel rescales the source target by \(M\sigma/2\), the capped one-arm source rate dominates the ambient radial term \(\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}\) with the explicit constant \(ab^2/128\).

items.label: Lemma lem:capped-exact-transport-package
items.nl:
For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) there are constants \(b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}},c_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}>0\) and a cutoff \(N_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathbb N\) with the following property.  For all integers \(n,d\ge1\), the capped exact alphabet size of \(\cref{obj:def:least-favorable-handle}\),
\[
d_{\mathrm{ex}}
:=
\min\left\{d,\ \max\left(1,\left\lfloor b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}n^2\right\rfloor\right)\right\},
\]
satisfies \(0<d_{\mathrm{ex}}\le d\), and satisfies \(d_{\mathrm{ex}}\le b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}n^2\) whenever \(N_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}\le n\).  Moreover there is a source level \(L_{\mathrm{ex}}=L_{\mathrm{ex}}(n,d)\) such that every measurable estimator \(\widehat\psi\) built from \(n\) binary records over \(d_{\mathrm{ex}}\) cells admits an exactly homogeneous binary law \(R\) with
\[
L_{\mathrm{ex}}
\le
E_{R^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\{\widehat\psi-\psi(R)\}^2\right],
\]
and such that, for every \(M\),
\[
c_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}M^2
\left\{\frac1n+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)\right\}
\le
M^2L_{\mathrm{ex}}.
\]
Thus the cited exact lower bound, its capped alphabet, and the small-sample parametric fallback are normalized into a single estimator-wise transport scale that is valid for every positive sample size and every ambient alphabet size.

items.label: Lemma lem:finite-sample-radial-transport-scale
items.nl:
Let \(N\ge1\) be a fixed sample-size cutoff, and let \(n\) and \(d\) be integers with \(1\le n\le N\).  Then, for every \(M\) and every \(\sigma\),
\[
\frac{1}{800N}\,M^2\sigma^2\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}
\le
\left(\frac{M\sigma}{2}\right)^2\frac1{200\,n}.
\]
Hence below the cutoff the one-arm two-point parametric source level \(1/(200n)\), rescaled by the Bernoulli radius-channel factor \(M\sigma/2\), already dominates the capped radial term, with the finite-sample constant \(c_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{small}}=1/(800N)\).

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: There are constants \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}>0\) and explicit estimators \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\) supplied by Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution}\) such that, uniformly for \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\), the total selector in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}estimator}\) obeys \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}-\tau(P))^2]\le C_{\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.\]

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl:
The two-sided bracket is matched at both required endpoints.  At \(\sigma=0\),
\[
 r_{n,d,0}=n^{-1}+\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)},\frac d{n^2}\right\}
 \asymp n^{-1}+\frac d{n^2}
\]
uniformly for \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\).  At \(\sigma=2\),
\(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}=\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) and
\[
 r_{n,d,2}=n^{-1}+\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\]
The lower expression in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:two\text{-}sided\text{-}minimax\text{-}bracket}\) is of the same order as these two rates at \(\sigma=0\) and \(\sigma=2\), respectively.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that, uniformly over \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\), the same model admits the radius-indexed lower bound
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{
 \frac1n+\frac d{n^2}+\sigma^2\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
The radius-dependent family is obtained by passing the fixed-sample binary one-arm hard experiment through the hypothesis-independent channel
\[
 B\longmapsto B'\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\frac12+\frac\sigma2\left(B-\frac12\right)\right),
 \qquad Y=M(B'-1/2).
\]
This construction has realization-wise radius at most \(\sigma M\) and preserves total-variation control by data processing.  It yields the natural product term \(\sigma^2\min\{1,d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\); it does not establish the stronger interior term \(\min\{\sigma^2,d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\).

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl:
Let \(\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) denote the binary-outcome class with arbitrary cell masses, fixed overlap \(\epsilon\), consistency, conditional exchangeability, and arm means in \([0,1]\), and let \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) be its uniform-mass, exactly homogeneous subclass.  The affine map
\[
 \Phi_M:\quad B(a)\longmapsto Y(a):=M\{B(a)-1/2\},\qquad Y=Y(A),
\]
embeds \(\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) into \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\), and embeds \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) into \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,0}\subseteq\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\).  The image is a strict subclass of the note's real-outcome class.  Restriction to the image of \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) transfers the lower term \(M^2(n^{-1}+d/n^2)\), while applying the hypothesis-independent channel in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:radius\text{-}channel\text{-}converse}\) to the binary one-arm hard family transfers the radius term
\[
 M^2\sigma^2\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\]
Thus the lower bounds arise by subclass restriction, whereas the explicit signed-mark upper estimator is proved on the broader real-outcome class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\).

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl:
The answer to the robust upper-construction question is affirmative.  For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the explicit linear-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}ratio\text{-}polynomial\text{-}upper}\) and the occupancy-weighted estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) in \(\mathrm{def:collision\text{-}handle}\) are elements of \(\mathcal T_{n,M}\).  There are \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that, for every \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(n^{-1}+\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\]
Both maps have explicit zero fallbacks and clipping, and neither bound contains an additional logarithmic factor.

items.label: Theorem T-7
items.nl:
Put \(L:=\log(en)\), \(b:=n^{-1}+d/n^2\), \(u:=d^2/(n^2L^2)\), and \(s:=\sigma^2\).  In the nonsaturated triangular regime \(L^2<d<nL\), the normalized selector and converse benchmarks
\[
 q:=\frac1n+\min\left\{u,s+\frac d{n^2}\right\},
 \qquad
 \ell:=b+su
\]
satisfy
\[
 \frac12\{b+\min(u,s)\}\le q\le b+\min(u,s),
 \qquad \ell=b+su.
\]
For every fixed \(\underline\sigma\in(0,2]\), there are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}\le C_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(\underline\sigma\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/L\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}
 \le \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
For every fixed \(C<\infty\), the same equivalence holds with constants independent of \(\sigma\in[0,2]\) whenever at least one of
\[
 u\ge1,
 \qquad u\le Cb,
 \qquad \sigma^2\le Cb
\]
holds.  The constant-free condition \(u\le b\) is exactly
\[
 d^2\le nL^2+dL^2.
\]
In particular, \(d\le\sqrt n\,L\) is sufficient, the former small-alphabet regime \(d\le L^2\) is retained, and matching holds for every admissible alphabet whenever \(\sigma^2\le C(n^{-1}+d/n^2)\).

Consequently, along a shrinking-radius sequence, the ratio of the current upper and lower benchmarks can diverge only in the residual wedge
\[
 b\ll u\ll1,
 \qquad
 b\ll\sigma^2\ll1.
\]
Up to boundary constants, this is \(\sqrt n\,L\ll d\ll nL\) together with \(\sigma^2\gg n^{-1}+d/n^2\).  The wedge is nonempty: for \(d_n=n\), \(L_n:=\log(en)\), and \(\sigma_n:=L_n^{-1/2}\), the selector benchmark divided by the proved lower benchmark satisfies
\[
 \frac{n^{-1}+\min\{1,d_n^2/(n^2L_n^2),\sigma_n^2+d_n/n^2\}}
 {n^{-1}+d_n/n^2+\sigma_n^2\min\{1,d_n^2/(n^2L_n^2)\}}
 \asymp L_n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus all endpoints, every fixed interior radius, saturation, the small-alphabet regime, and both parametric-dominance elbows are matched.  Only the displayed residual wedge can require a stronger constrained converse or a sharper estimator; neither endpoint-only reasoning nor the existing radius channel decides between them.

items.label: Theorem T-8
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon}\le C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(0\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/\log(en)\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}+\sigma^2\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}
 \le\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
Both inequalities hold on the same real-outcome, arbitrary-cell-mass class.  This is a two-sided minimax bracket, not a claim that the two displayed benchmarks are uniformly order-equivalent at every shrinking interior radius.

The accepted-bank theorem \texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap\_polynomial\_upper\_match/thm:sharp-minimax-fixed-interior} establishes the unrestricted binary-outcome hybrid rate \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\).  The present theorem is not a restatement of that endpoint: on one arbitrary-cell-mass real-outcome class under conditional-second-central-moment control, it gives a known-radius upper and lower minimax bracket.  Its increment is the radius-indexed same-class bracket, the explicit weak-moment signed-mark construction and known-radius selector, the radius-channel converse, and the localization of every remaining possible mismatch to the explicit shrinking-radius wedge in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:fixed\text{-}interior\text{-}tightness\text{-}and\text{-}shrinking\text{-}radius\text{-}gap}\); real outcomes alone are not claimed as novel.

items.label: Theorem T-9
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is a constant \(c_{\epsilon}>0\) such that, uniformly over every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\) and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\),
\[
 \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \ge c_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{
 \frac1n+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)
 +\sigma^2\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
The radius component passes the fixed-sample binary one-arm hard experiment through the hypothesis-independent channel
\[
 B\longmapsto B'\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\frac12+\frac\sigma2\left(B-\frac12\right)\right),
 \qquad Y=M(B'-1/2),
\]
and embeds the source construction on a capped number of positive-mass cells when \(d\) exceeds its source range.  The construction has realization-wise radius at most \(\sigma M\) and preserves total-variation control by data processing.  It proves the product radius term displayed above, not the stronger interior term \(\min\{\sigma^2,d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\).

items.label: Theorem T-10
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the explicit linear-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) and the occupancy-weighted estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) are total elements of \(\mathcal T_{n,M}\).  A constant \(C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) satisfies, for every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\) and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(n^{-1}+\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\]
Both maps have explicit zero fallbacks and clipping, and neither bound contains an additional logarithmic factor.

items.label: Theorem T-11
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the total known-radius selector \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}\) in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}estimator}\) satisfies, for a constant \(C_{\epsilon}<\infty\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}-\tau(P))^2]
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}
\]
for every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\) and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\).

items.label: Theorem T-12
items.nl:
The all-alphabet two-sided bracket is matched at exact and unrestricted homogeneity.  For every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\), at \(\sigma=0\),
\[
 r_{n,d,0}=n^{-1}+\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)},\frac d{n^2}\right\}
 \asymp n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right).
\]
At \(\sigma=2\), \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}=\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) and
\[
 r_{n,d,2}=n^{-1}+\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\]
The capped lower expression in Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:two\text{-}sided\text{-}minimax\text{-}bracket\text{-}all\text{-}d}\) is of the same order as these two rates at \(\sigma=0\) and \(\sigma=2\), respectively, uniformly over all \(d\ge1\).

items.label: Theorem T-13
items.nl:
Put \(L:=\log(en)\), \(b:=n^{-1}+d/n^2\), \(u:=d^2/(n^2L^2)\), and \(s:=\sigma^2\).  In the nonsaturated triangular regime \(L^2<d<nL\), the normalized selector and converse benchmarks
\[
 q:=\frac1n+\min\left\{u,s+\frac d{n^2}\right\},
 \qquad
 \ell:=b+su
\]
satisfy
\[
 \frac12\{b+\min(u,s)\}\le q\le b+\min(u,s),
 \qquad \ell=b+su.
\]
For every fixed \(\underline\sigma\in(0,2]\), there are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}\le C_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(\underline\sigma\le\sigma\le2\) and every integer \(d\ge1\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}
 \le \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
For every fixed \(C<\infty\), the same equivalence holds with constants independent of \(\sigma\in[0,2]\) whenever at least one of
\[
 u\ge1,
 \qquad u\le Cb,
 \qquad \sigma^2\le Cb
\]

\[

\]

Consequently, along a shrinking-radius sequence, the ratio of the all-alphabet upper and lower benchmarks can diverge only in the residual wedge
\[
 b\ll u\ll1,
 \qquad
 b\ll\sigma^2\ll1.
\]

\[
 \frac{n^{-1}+\min\{1,d_n^2/(n^2L_n^2),\sigma_n^2+d_n/n^2\}}

items.label: Theorem T-14
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon}\le C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\) and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon}M^2\left\{\frac1n+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)+\sigma^2\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}
 \le\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
Both inequalities hold on the same arbitrary-cell-mass real-outcome class under fixed overlap, the conditional-mean normalization, and the conditional-second-central-moment envelope.  This is an all-alphabet two-sided minimax bracket, not a claim that the two displayed benchmarks are uniformly order-equivalent at every shrinking interior radius.

The accepted-bank theorem \texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap\_polynomial\_upper\_match/thm:sharp-minimax-fixed-interior} establishes the unrestricted binary-outcome hybrid rate \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\).  The present theorem is not a restatement of that endpoint.  Its increment is the all-alphabet radius-indexed same-class bracket, the explicit weak-moment signed-mark construction and known-radius selector, the capped exact-homogeneity and radius-channel embeddings, and localization of every remaining possible mismatch to the shrinking-radius wedge; real outcomes alone are not claimed as novel.

items.label: Theorem thm:published-binary-collision-comparison
items.nl: Conditional on the published binary collision guarantee of Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, the selector frontier's heterogeneity-dependent remainder is never larger than the published collision remainder, and it is strictly smaller when \(d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]=o(\sigma^2+d/n^2)\) and \(d=o(n\log(en))\).

items.label: Cited result lem:zeng-binary-collision-upper
items.nl:
In the binary-outcome model of Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, let \(\psi:=\sum_{k=1}^dp_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\), let \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}:=\max_{1\le k\le d}|\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k}-\psi|\), and let \(\widehat\psi_{\mathrm{col}}\) be their occupancy-weighted estimator in equation (13).  Under overlap \(\epsilon\), their Theorem 3 states
\[
 |E(\widehat\psi_{\mathrm{col}}-\psi)|
 \le \sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}+2\exp\left\{-C(\epsilon)\frac{n^2}{n\vee d}\right\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\widehat\psi_{\mathrm{col}})
 \lesssim_{\epsilon}\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}^2+\frac d{n^2}+\frac1n.
\]
